payload.stem: If we substitute number 1 to 12 indicating hours on the dial clock by letters of the alphabet in their order starting with C, which letter would represent 8 ?

items.rule: 1 is C, so 8 is seven letters on: J.

payload.stem: Through how many degrees does the hour hand in a clock move as the time changes from 3 hours and 36 minutes to 6 hours ?

items.rule: From 3:36 to 6:00 is 144 minutes; the hour hand turns ½° a minute: 72°.

payload.stem: The priest told the devotee, "The bell rings at regular intervals of 45 minutes. The last bell rang 5 minutes ago. The next bell is due to be rung at 7:45 am.' At what time did the priest give this information to the devotee ?

items.rule: The last bell rang 45 minutes before 7:45, at 7:00; five minutes later is 7:05 am.

payload.stem: Rakesh put his timepiece on the table in such a way that at 6 PM the hour hand points to North, then in which direction will the minute hand point at 9.15 PM'?

items.rule: The 6 faces North, so going clockwise the 9 faces East, the 12 South and the 3 West. At 9:15 the minute hand is on the 3: West.

payload.stem: A clock shows time 7:30 hrs. If the minute needle shows the West, then what will be direction of the hour needle ?

items.rule: At 7:30 the minute hand is on the 6, facing West. The hour hand, halfway between 7 and 8, is 45° clockwise of it: North-West.

payload.stem:
Choose the correct alternative from the given options :
If 8th of April falls on Monday, what Day would be the 30th May of that year ?

items.rule: 30 May is 22 + 30 = 52 days after 8 April: 7 weeks + 3 days, so Monday + 3 = Thursday.

payload.stem: If the seventh day of a month is three days earlier than Friday. What day will it be on the nineteenth day of the month ?

items.rule: The 7th is Tuesday; the 19th is 12 days later, 1 week + 5 days: Sunday.

payload.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand when it is 5 : 10 pm ?
If in the year 2012, January 1st is Sunday, then which day is the Indian Republic Day in the year 2012 ?

items.rule: 26 January is 25 days after 1 January: 3 weeks + 4 days, so Sunday + 4 = Thursday.

payload.stem: If 30th January 2003 was Thursday, what was the day on 2nd March, 2003 ?

items.rule: 2 March 2003 is 31 days after 30 January: 4 weeks + 3 days, so Thursday + 3 = Sunday.

payload.stem: If 1st October is Sunday, then 1st November will be :

items.rule: October has 31 days: 4 weeks + 3, so Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.

payload.stem: Which among the following year is a leap year ?

items.rule: A century year is a leap year only when it divides by 400: 2800.

payload.stem: What is the angle between the two hands of a clock when the time is 15 minutes past 4 O' clock ?
Find the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock when it is 38 minutes past 7 pm.

items.note: The minute count sits on the page curl and is read as 38.

payload.stem: An accurate clock shows 8 O' clock in the morning. Through how many degrees will the hour hand rotate when the clock shows 2 O' clock in the afternoon ?

items.rule: Six hours at 30° an hour: 180°.

payload.stem: The reflex angle between the hands of a clock at 10 : 25 is :

items.rule: At 10:25 the hands are |300 − 137.5| = 162.5° apart; the reflex angle is 360 − 162.5 = 197½°.

payload.stem: A clock is started at noon. By 10 minutes past 5, the hour hand has turned through :

items.rule: Noon to 5:10 is 310 minutes, at ½° a minute: 155°.

payload.stem: The angle between the minute hand and the hour hand of a clock when the time is 4 : 20, is :
At what angle the hands of a clock are inclined at 15 minutes past 5 ?
How many times are the hands of a clock at right angle in a day ?

items.rule: The hands are at right angles twice in every 12/11 hours, so 2 × 22 = 44 times in a day.

payload.stem: The angle between the minute hand and the hour hand of a clock when the time is 8 : 30, is :
A father says to his son, I was thrice as old as you are at your birth. If the present age of the father is 48 years, then what was the age of the son 4 years ago ?

items.rule: At the son's birth the father was three times the son's present age: 48 − s = 3s, so s = 12, and 4 years ago he was 8.

payload.stem: The sum of the ages of Reena and her father is 60 and the difference between their ages is 36. Find the age of Reena's father.

items.rule: Father + Reena = 60 and father − Reena = 36, so the father is (60 + 36) ÷ 2 = 48.

payload.stem: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 3 : 5. After 7 years B's age will be double of C's age. If C celebrated his 10th birthday 4 years ago, then what is the present age (in years) of A?

items.rule: C is 10 + 4 = 14, so 21 in 7 years; B will then be 42, so B is 35 now and A is 3/5 of it: 21.

payload.stem: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 4 : 5. After 5 years the age of B will be 35 years. What is the present age (in years) of A?

items.rule: B is 35 − 5 = 30, so A is 4/5 of it: 24.

payload.stem: The ratio of the present ages of Richa and her husband is 3 : 4. Five years from now, the ratio of the ages of her husband and son will be 3 : 1. If the present age of Richa is 21 years, then what will be the present age (in years) of her son?

items.rule: Richa is 21, so her husband is 28 and will be 33 in five years; the son will then be 11, so he is 6 now.

payload.stem: The present age of A is twice that of B. B's age after 5 years. will be 4 times the present age of C. If C celebrated his seventh birthday 4 years ago, then what will be the present age (in years) of A?

items.rule: C is 7 + 4 = 11; B + 5 = 44, so B is 39 and A is 78.

payload.stem: The present age of A is 52 years. After 8 years the ratio of the ages of A and B will be 4 : 5. What is the present age (in years) of B?

items.rule: A will be 60 in 8 years; 60 : B = 4 : 5 makes B 75 then, 67 now.

payload.stem: 4 years ago, A was twice as old as B. After 6 years C's age will be twice of A's age. Present age of A. is 10 years more than the present age of B. What is the present age of C?
The ratio of the age of the father to the age of the son is 5 : 2. If the product of their ages is 160, then what is the age of the father?

items.rule: 5k × 2k = 160 gives k = 4: the father is 20.

payload.stem: Amit is 6 years younger than Arjun. If the ratio of the ages of Amit and Arjun is 5 : 7, then what is the age (in years) of Amit?

items.rule: 7k − 5k = 6 gives k = 3: Amit is 15.

payload.stem: The present age of Ashok is twice the present age of Kishan. After 7 years, Kishan's age will be 4 times of Karthik's present age. If karthik celebrated his 9th birthday 3 years ago, then What is the present age of Ashok ?

items.rule: Karthik is 9 + 3 = 12; Kishan + 7 = 48, so Kishan is 41 and Ashok 82.

payload.stem: Manoj starts from his home and reaches the temple in 7 hours, he travels 1/4th of the total distance at a speed of 10km/h and the remaining distance at 12km/h. Find the distance between his home and the temple.

items.rule: d/4 at 10 km/h and 3d/4 at 12 km/h take d/40 + d/16 = 7d/80 hours = 7, so d = 80 km.

payload.stem: If a car covers a distance of 210 km in 3 hours and 30 minutes, then what is the average speed of the car in kmph?

items.rule: 210 km in 3.5 hours is 60 km/h.

payload.stem: Train A, which runs at a speed of 90 km/h, starts from Station Y at 8 a.m. Train B, which runs at a speed of 120 km/h, starts from Station Y on the same route at 8.10 a.m.. If Train B catches up with Train A at 8.40 a.m. at Station Z, then what is the distance between Stations Y and Z ?

items.rule: By 8.40 Train A has run 40 minutes at 90 km/h and Train B 30 minutes at 120 km/h: 60 km each.

payload.stem: When the price of petrol was increased by 25%, Yogesh reduced his journey so that his monthly expenditure on petrol remained the same as before. By what percent did Yogesh cut down his journey?

items.rule: Spending the same at 1.25 times the price buys 1 ÷ 1.25 = 0.8 as much: a 20% cut.

payload.stem: In a class of 45 students, all the students participate in either one or both of the games Chess and Badminton. 11 students participate in both the games, while 17 students participate in only Chess. Find the total number of students who participated in Badminton.

items.rule: Everyone plays at least one: 45 − 17 who play only chess = 28 play badminton.

payload.stem: A student has to obtain 40% of the maximum marks in order to pass. If she scored 80 marks and still failed by 20 marks, then calculate the maximum marks?

items.rule: The pass mark is 80 + 20 = 100 = 40% of the maximum: 250.

payload.stem: If the price of a product is first decreased by 35% and then increased by 20%, what will be the net change in the price of the product?

items.rule: 0.65 × 1.2 = 0.78: the price falls by 22%.

payload.stem: Sunita appeared for a test consisting of 260 questions and answered 40% of the first 130 questions correctly. What percentage of the rest 130 questions must she answer correctly so as to score 60% in the entire test ?

items.rule: 60% of 260 is 156; she has 40% of 130 = 52, so needs 104 of the last 130: 80%.

payload.stem: When a number is subtracted from the square of 25, it becomes 124 times of the number. Find the number.

items.rule: 625 − x = 124x gives x = 5.

payload.stem: When twice of a number added to 3 is multiplied by 5 and added to the number itself, it gives 158. What is the square of that number ?
A book has 300 pages and each page has 20 lines of 10-10 words each. How many words are there in the book ?

items.rule: 300 pages × 20 lines × 10 words = 60,000.
items.note: "10-10 words" is read as 10 words to a line.

payload.stem: The last three digits of the binary equivalent of the number 85432578 are :

items.rule: The last three binary digits are the remainder by 8: 578 leaves 2, which is 010.

payload.stem: The average income of six friends A, B, C, D, E and F is ₹ 6,500. The total income of B, D, E and F is ₹ 25,000. If A's income is ₹ 4,000 less than that of C, then find C's income.

items.rule: Six incomes total 39,000; A + C = 14,000 and C = A + 4,000, so C is ₹ 9,000.

payload.stem: The average weight of 8 students is 57 kg. Their individual weights are 55 kg, 49 kg, 57 kg, 63 kg, 68 kg, 52 kg, X kg and Y kg respectively. What is the sum of X and Y?

items.rule: The eight weigh 456 kg; the six named weigh 344 kg, so X + Y = 112 kg.

payload.stem: A fruit shop consists of only two types of fruits namely oranges and mangoes. The number of oranges is three times the number of mangoes. Which of the following number CANNOT represent the total number of fruits in the shop?

items.rule: Oranges and mangoes make 3m + m = 4m: the total divides by 4, and only 42 does not.

payload.stem:
What is the difference between the largest and the smallest of the following fractions?
4/5, 5/6, 3/8, 5/7, 6/7

items.rule: The largest is 6/7 and the smallest 3/8: 48/56 − 21/56 = 27/56.

payload.stem: An amount of Rs. 1,189 is to be divided among Rakesh, Mrinal and Sanjay in the ratio of 11:13:17, respectively. How much amount will Sanjay get more than Rakesh?

items.rule: 1,189 ÷ 41 parts = 29 a part; Sanjay gets 17 − 11 = 6 parts more: ₹174.

payload.stem: A certain sum of money was divided among Darshan, Swati and Nivriti. Out of that Nivriti got ₹ 539. If the ratio of the money distributed among Darshan, Swati and Nivruti is 5:6:7, then what was the total money distributed?

items.rule: 7 parts are ₹ 539, so a part is 77 and the 18 parts total ₹ 1,386.

payload.stem: A sum of Rs 6,764 is to be distributed among four friends P, Q R and S in the ratio 8 : 6 : 3 : 2. What is the total amount that P and R together will get?

items.rule: 6,764 ÷ 19 parts = 356 a part; P and R have 8 + 3 = 11 parts: ₹ 3,916.

payload.stem: There are two numbers. The difference between the two numbers is 2 and the difference between their squares is 8. Find the value of these two numbers?

items.rule: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) = 8 with a − b = 2, so a + b = 4: 3 and 1.

payload.stem: A drum contains 40 litres of milk. One-fourth of the milk is taken out and replaced with water. Then, half of the mixture is taken out and replaced with water. What is the respective quantity of milk and water left in the drum ?

items.rule: Taking out a quarter leaves 30 l of milk; taking out half leaves 15 l. The drum is topped up to 40 l: 15 l milk, 25 l water.

payload.stem: ₹ 2,871 is to be divided among A, B and C in the ratio of 9 : 11 : 13 respectively. How much more money (in ₹) will C get than A?

items.rule: 2,871 ÷ 33 parts = 87 a part; C gets 13 − 9 = 4 parts more: ₹ 348.

payload.stem: The present age of a father is three times that of his son. Son's age after 10 years will be 5 times of Raman's present age. If Raman celebrated his third birthday 2 years ago, then what is the present age (in years) of the father?

items.rule: Raman is 3 + 2 = 5; the son will be 25 in 10 years, so is 15, and the father 45.

payload.stem: Saksham's present age is one-third of his father's present age. 5 years ago Saksham's father's age was half of Saksham's grandfather's age. If Saksham's grandfather will celebrate his 88th birthday after 3 years, then what is the present age (in years) of Saksham?

items.rule: The grandfather is 85, 80 five years ago; the father was 40 then, 45 now, and Saksham is 15.

payload.stem: The ratio of the present ages of Sumit and Amit is 3 : 4. If Sumit's age after 20 years will be 62 years, then what is Amit's present age (in years)?

items.rule: Sumit is 62 − 20 = 42 = 3 parts, so Amit is 4 parts: 56.

payload.stem: Among the four friends, Govind is twice the age of Krishna. Nandu is half of Krishna's age. Gwala is 6 years older than Krishna, but 6 years younger than Govind. Who is the youngest in age?

items.rule: Gwala = K + 6 = 2K − 6 gives Krishna 12, Govind 24, Gwala 18 and Nandu 6: Nandu is the youngest.

payload.stem: Mona is 6 years younger to her husband and her husband's age is five times that of their daughter Reena. If Reena was 5 years old 3 years ago, then what is the present age of Mona?

items.rule: Reena is 8, her father 40, and Mona 6 years younger: 34.

payload.stem: 15 chains were bought for ₹7,520 and sold for ₹9,450. What is the approximate profit percentage per chain?

items.rule: Profit 1,930 on 7,520 is 25.7%: about 26%.

payload.stem: Neha wants to sell an item. If he wants to make a profit of 200%, then the selling price should be how many times the cost price?

items.rule: A 200% profit adds twice the cost: the price is 3 times the cost.

payload.stem: The difference between the simple interest and the compound interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹ 732. Find the amount.

items.rule: Over two years the gap is P × 10% × 10% = P/100 = 732, so P = ₹ 73,200.

payload.stem: Among five objects E, F, G, H and K, the weight of H is three times that of K. The weight of G is 7.5 kg. The weight of E is twice the weight of F. The weight of K is four times the weight of G. If the weight of F is the same as that of G, then which is the second heavier object?

items.rule: G = F = 7.5, E = 15, K = 30, H = 90: K is second heaviest.

payload.stem: Among five things named K, L, M, N and O, the weight of M is 60 kg. The weight of L is twice that of N. The weight of O is thrice that of L. The weight of K is half that of O. If the weight of K is equal to that of M, then what is the weight of N?

items.rule: K = M = 60, so O = 120, L = 40 and N = 20 kg.

payload.stem: There are three books coded as A, B and C. The price of book A is twice the price of book B and one-third the price of book C. If book C costs ₹ 84, then what are the costs of book A and book B, respectively ?

items.rule: A is a third of 84, ₹ 28, and B half of A, ₹ 14.

payload.stem: There are 12 dozens of apples in a basket. Two dozens are added later. Ten apples got spoiled and are removed. The remaining are transferred equally into two baskets, how many are in each ?

items.rule: 14 dozen = 168, less 10 spoiled = 158, split in two: 79.

payload.stem: On a farm there are 48 ducks, 42 goats and 10 cows including some attendants. If the total number of legs is 216 more than the number of heads, then what is the number of attendants on the form?

items.rule: Animals have 100 heads and 96 + 168 + 40 = 304 legs; each attendant adds 1 head and 2 legs. 304 + 2a = 100 + a + 216 gives a = 12.

payload.stem: 390625 is at which position in the series 5, 25, 125, 625, ............ ?

items.rule: 390625 = 5⁸: the 8th term.

payload.stem: A father tells his son, "I was three times of your present age when you were born." If the father's present age is 48 years, how old was the boy 4 years ago ?

items.rule: As Q1: 48 − s = 3s gives s = 12, so 4 years ago he was 8.

payload.stem: If a train 150 m long crosses a pole in 12 seconds, then what is the speed of the train in km/hr ?

items.rule: 150 m in 12 s is 12.5 m/s = 45 km/h.

payload.stem: What number is as much more than 10 as it is less than one half of that from which 50 is 10 less?

items.rule: 50 is 10 less than 60, and half of 60 is 30. x − 10 = 30 − x gives 20.

payload.stem: 6 years ago, Raju's age was 2 years less than half his brother's age, which was 20 years. What is his present age?

items.rule: Six years ago Raju was 20 ÷ 2 − 2 = 8; now he is 14.

payload.stem: Mother was three times the age of her daughter five years ago. After five years, mother will be twice as old as her daughter. How old is the daughter today ?
The age of a father is thrice that of his son. If the sum of their ages is 48 years, what is the age of the father ?

items.rule: Son + 3 × son = 48: the son is 12, the father 36.

payload.stem: The sum of the squares of the digits of the largest prime number in two digits is :

items.rule: The largest two-digit prime is 97: 81 + 49 = 130.

payload.stem: Find the number lying between 900 and 1000 which when divided by 38 and 57 leaves in each case a remainder of 23.

items.rule: The LCM of 38 and 57 is 114; 114 × 8 + 23 = 935 is the one between 900 and 1000.

payload.stem: Raju can do a piece of work in 20 days, while Ram can do it in 30 days. If both of them work at it together, then the number of days in which they will be able to finish the work is :

items.rule: Together they do 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 a day: 12 days.

payload.stem: There are 2000 students in a school. 10 per cent of these students travel to school by car, 40 per cent of the students travel by bus. How many students of that school walk to school?

items.rule: 10% go by car and 40% by bus; the other 50% walk: 1000.

payload.stem: In a money bag there are ₹ 1 coins, ₹ 2 coins and ₹ 5 coins. If the ratio of the number of coins be 4 : 3 : 2 and the total money in the bag is ₹ 500, the amount of money in ₹ 2 denomination is :

items.rule: 4k × 1 + 3k × 2 + 2k × 5 = 20k = 500, so k = 25: 75 two-rupee coins make ₹150.

payload.stem: The average of 5 consecutive odd positive integers is 9. The least one among them is :

items.rule: Five consecutive odd numbers averaging 9: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.

payload.stem: In a department, 24 employees know typing and 11 know stenography, 25 know how to use a computer. 7 know both typing and stenography, 4 know stenography and computers, 12 know typing and computers and 3 know all the three. If there were 50 employees in the department, find how many employees don't know any of the three jobs.

items.rule: At least one skill: 24 + 11 + 25 − 7 − 4 − 12 + 3 = 40, so 50 − 40 = 10 know none.

payload.stem: An official meeting is attended by 130 department employees. Of them, 66 drink tea, 56 drink coffee and 63 drink juice, 27 can drink either tea or coffee. 25 can drink coffee or juice and 23 can drink juice and tea, 5 employees can drink any of the three. How many drink only tea ?

items.rule: Only tea = 66 − 27 (tea and coffee) − 23 (juice and tea) + 5 (all three) = 21.
items.note: "either tea or coffee" and "coffee or juice" are read as both, as the counts only make sense that way.

payload.stem: Joel and Tom were travelling from Town X to Town Y which was 210 km apart. Joel set off 1 h 15 min later than Tom but arrived 15 min earlier. If the average speed of Tom was 42 km/h, find the average speed of Joel.

items.rule: Tom took 210 ÷ 42 = 5 h; Joel took 5 − 1¼ − ¼ = 3½ h: 60 km/h.

payload.stem: A bus driver wants to travel a distance of 200 km. He travels with the speed of 40 km/h. He takes rest at 3 different hotels for 15 min, 30 min and 15 min, respectively. He starts his journey at 9:00 am. At what time does he reach his final destination ?

items.rule: 200 ÷ 40 = 5 hours of driving and 1 hour of rest: 9:00 am + 6 h = 3 : 00 pm.

payload.stem: Town A and town B were 600 km apart. Joshua left town A for town B and travelled at an average speed of 65 km/h. At the same time, Menon left town B for town A. The two of them meet 5 h later. Find Menon's average speed.

items.rule: Together they close 600 km in 5 h, 120 km/h; Menon makes 120 − 65 = 55.

payload.stem: While Suresh set out on a journey he found that the tank of his scooter was 2/3 full. After riding for some hours, he spent 3 litres and lent his friend another 3 litres of petrol. Suresh then found that he had 1/6th of the tank full. What was the full capacity of his petrol tank ?

items.rule: 2/3 − 1/6 = 1/2 of the tank is 6 litres: 12 litres.

payload.stem: Present ages of father and son are in the ratio of 5 : 1, respectively. 7 yr. later, this ratio becomes 3 : 1. What is the son's present age (in yr.) ?

items.rule: 5s + 7 = 3(s + 7) gives s = 7.

payload.stem: Mani is double the age of Prabhu. Ramona is half the age of Prabhu. If Mani is sixty, find out the age of Ramona.

items.rule: Prabhu is 30, Ramona half that: 15.

payload.stem: Your mother is 4 years younger than your father who is six times older than you. If your age is 6 years, what is your mother's age ?

items.rule: The father is 6 × 6 = 36, the mother 4 younger: 32.

payload.stem: An accurate clock shows 8 O' clock in the morning. Through how many degrees will the hour hand rotate when the clock shows 2 O' clock in the afternoon ?

items.rule: Six hours at 30° an hour: 180°.

payload.stem: The sum of ages of mother, daughter and son is 87 yr. What will be the sum of their ages after 8 yr. ?

items.rule: Three people each 8 years older: 87 + 24 = 111.

payload.stem: The age of Sunita's father today is four times as that of her age. After 8 years, the age of her father will be three times that of her age. What is Sunita's age today ?
Ramesh got some mangoes among which the ripe ones were 3 times the raw ones. If he got 68 mangoes in all, how many of them were raw ?

items.rule: Raw + 3 × raw = 68: 17 raw.

payload.stem: There are ostriches and zebras in a zoo. By counting their heads they are 40 and the number of their legs is 100. How many ostriches are there ?

items.rule: 40 heads and 100 legs: z = (100 − 80) ÷ 2 = 10 zebras, so 30 ostriches.

payload.stem: In a retail shop, there were 54 cupboards. In each cupboard, 28 racks were made. In each rack, 10 boxes were kept. In each box, 4 shirts were packed. One day 500 boxes were sold and 250 boxes were purchased. How many shirts were there on that day ?

items.rule: 54 × 28 × 10 × 4 = 60,480 shirts; 250 boxes fewer is 1,000 shirts fewer: 59,480.

payload.stem: In a row, 25 trees are planted at equal distance from each other. The distance between 1st and 25th tree is 30 m. What is the distance between 3rd and 15th tree ?

items.rule: 24 gaps make 30 m, 1.25 m each; 3rd to 15th is 12 gaps: 15 m.

payload.stem: In a class composed of x girls and y boys what part of the class is composed of girls?

items.rule: Girls over the whole class: x/(x + y).

payload.stem: If a number is greater than 5 but less than 9 and greater than 7 but less than 11, the number is :

items.rule: Between 5 and 9 and between 7 and 11 leaves only 8.

payload.stem: Mahesh is 60 yr. old. Ram is 5 yrs. junior to Mahesh and 4 yrs. senior to Raju. The youngest brother of Raju is Babu and he is 6 yrs. junior to him. What is the age difference between Mahesh and Babu ?

items.rule: Ram is 55, Raju 51, Babu 45: 60 − 45 = 15.

payload.stem: There were 120 tigers in the sanctuary. 20% of them were killed by unknown hunters. 50% of the remaining died in fire in the sanctuary. How many tigers are there in the sanctuary now ?

items.rule: 120 less 20% is 96; half of those died: 48.

payload.stem: Two cubes have volumes in the ratio 1 : 27. The ratio of the face of one to that of the other is :

items.rule: Volumes 1 : 27 mean sides 1 : 3 and faces 1 : 9.

payload.stem: Two buses start at the same time from Delhi and Agra, which are 300 km apart, towards each other. After what time will they cross each other if their speeds are 38 km/hr and 37km/hr respectively?

items.rule: They close at 75 km/h: 300 km in 4 hours.

payload.stem: Ravi has spent a quarter (1/4) of his life as a boy, one-fifth (1/5) as a youth, one-third (1/3) as a man and 13 yrs. in old age. What is his present age ?

items.rule: 1/4 + 1/5 + 1/3 = 47/60, so 13 years is 13/60 of his life: 60 years.

payload.stem: A husband and a wife had five married sons and each of them had four children. How many members are there in the family ?

items.rule: Husband and wife, five sons, their five wives and twenty children: 32.

payload.stem: The average age of 25 subordinates in an office is 30 yr. If the age of Manager is added, the average increases to 31 yr. What is the age of the Manager ?
Find the lowest number which when divided by 8,12,15 and 20 leaves the remainder 2.
A group of 1500 persons consisting of captains and soldiers is travelling in a train. For every 19 soldiers there is one captain. The number of captains in the group is :

items.rule: One captain in every 20 people: 1500 ÷ 20 = 75.

payload.stem: There are some balls of red, green and yellow colour lying on a table. There are as many as red balls as there are yellow balls. There are twice as many yellow balls as there are green ones. The number of red balls :

options.A: is equal to the sum of yellow and green balls.
options.B: is double the number of green balls.
options.C: is equal to yellow balls minus green balls.

items.rule: Red = yellow = 2 × green, so red is double the green.

payload.stem: Sea animals, Shripm, Walrus

options.A: Three circles, one inside the next
options.B: A circle inside another, and a third circle apart from both
options.C: Two separate circles inside a larger one
options.D: Three separate circles in a row

payload.direction: Select the venn diagram that best represents the relationship between the following classes. And select the set of classes whose relationship between them is best represented by the following ven diagram.

items.rule: Shrimps and walruses are both sea animals, and no shrimp is a walrus: two separate circles inside a larger one.

payload.stem:
Doctor, Professor, Cardiologist
1=doctor, 2=coardiologist, 3=Professor

options.A: Circle 2 inside circle 1, and circle 3 crossing both
options.B: Circle 2 inside circle 1, and circle 3 apart from both
options.C: Circles 2, 1 and 3 in a chain: 1 overlaps the other two, which do not meet

payload.direction: Select the venn diagram that best represents the relationship between the following classes. And select the set of classes whose relationship between them is best represented by the following ven diagram.

items.rule: Every cardiologist (2) is a doctor (1); some doctors are professors (3), and some professors are cardiologists: 2 inside 1, and 3 crossing both.

payload.stem: Girls, Healthy, Trains

options.A: Two overlapping circles, and a third touching both, in a square
options.B: Three circles, each touching the other two, in a square
